top_news.title: trajectory-judge: What Outcome-Only LLM Judges Miss on Agent Trajectories
top_news.dek: Outcome-only evaluation fails to detect agent errors that result in correct final answers but follow flawed execution paths.
top_news.brief: Researchers demonstrate that standard LLM evaluation, which only checks final outputs, misses 'silent' failures where agents reach the correct result through incorrect tool usage. By using a deterministic environment with fault injection, the study highlights the need for process-aware evaluation to ensure agent reliability.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing the difference between outcome-only and process-aware evaluation paths.

top_news.title: datasette-mcp 0.2
top_news.dek: Datasette-mcp 0.2 adds an MCP server endpoint to any Datasette instance, improving model compatibility.
top_news.brief: The update introduces a /-/mcp endpoint, allowing Datasette instances to function as Model Context Protocol servers. It also updates the SQL execution output to return an array of objects rather than arrays, helping LLMs better map data to column names.
top_news.image_alt: Datasette logo and MCP protocol icon.

top_news.title: Cloudflare Adds Optional OAuth Scopes, Letting Developers Mark What Users May Decline
top_news.dek: Cloudflare now supports optional OAuth scopes, allowing users to deselect specific permissions during consent.
top_news.brief: To address the broad permission requests typical of AI agents, Cloudflare allows developers to mark specific OAuth scopes as optional. This gives users granular control over what an agent can access, mitigating the 'all-or-nothing' consent problem for MCP servers and other agentic tools.
top_news.image_alt: UI mockup of an OAuth consent screen with optional checkboxes.

top_news.title: The efficient frontier of LLM inference
top_news.dek: The efficient frontier framework helps developers navigate the trade-offs between LLM latency, throughput, and cost.
top_news.brief: This analysis applies the economic concept of the 'efficient frontier' to LLM inference. It provides a framework for evaluating model performance, helping teams identify the optimal balance of intelligence and resource consumption for specific production workloads.
top_news.image_alt: Graph illustrating the efficient frontier curve for LLM inference trade-offs.

top_news.title: BenchMIRT: What are LLM benchmarks actually measuring?
top_news.dek: BenchMIRT provides a method to audit LLM benchmarks at the individual prompt level to identify what they truly measure.
top_news.brief: BenchMIRT allows researchers to deconstruct benchmarks into individual tasks, revealing hidden dependencies—such as reasoning or entity tracking—that influence scores beyond the stated goal. This approach enables the creation of more focused, interpretable evaluations.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual diagram of BenchMIRT auditing individual benchmark prompts.

primary.title: REAL-Q: E2E LLM Quantization via Dynamic Gradient Descent
primary.summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is essential for deploying large language models (LLMs) under strict resource constraints.
